turns.note: First split: C4- from C5+ to see costs and splits.
Tune first split toward C4-/C5+ cut (1168 mol/s tops).
Build full direct-sequence tree: C3/C4 blends, C5 blend, C6 paraffin blend (with MCP), cyclohexane, heptane, octane, nonane.
Sharpen light splits; restructure heavy end: BBB splits CH+C7 / C8+C9, then CH/heptane and octane/nonane.
Sharpen C3/C4, C4/C5, C5/C6 and C7/C8 splits to make C4, C5, C6-paraffin blends and octane sellable.
Go back to the best design (turn 4) to look at its stream compositions before changing anything else.
Sharpen C4/C5 (feed col), C3/C4 (T) and C5/C6 (B) splits to make C4 mix, C5 mix and C6 paraffin blend sellable.
Return to best design (turn 4) to view its stream compositions and costs before tuning.
Shift feed cut to push butane overhead, push more C3 overhead in T, sharpen C5/C6 in B, aiming for C4, C5, C6 blends.
Return to the best design (turn 4) and look at its streams before making changes one at a time.
Sharpen C4/C5 (feed) and C5/C6 (B) splits holding the cut points near ideal, aiming for C5 mix in BT and C6 paraffin blend in BBT (worth ~$700M and ~$980M).
Return to best design (turn 4) to read its stream compositions in full before tuning a single column.
Push more propane overhead in T (C4 mix in TB), sharpen C5/C6 in B with more stages and slight more boilup to strip pentane out of BBT.
Push the remaining ~36 mol/s butane overhead in the feed column so BT (iC5+nC5 at 94%) reaches the 95% C5 mix spec, worth about $690M/yr.
Push residual butane overhead in feed column (C5 mix in BT), more propane overhead in T (C4 mix in TB), push heptane overhead in BBB so octane/nonane split cleanly.
C6 paraffin blend in BBT (~$900M/yr) is at 91%: add stages/reflux to BB. Also sharpen T (C3 mix), BBB, BBBT (CH/heptane), BBBB (C8/C9).
Push remaining propane overhead in T (C4 mix in TB); push heptane up in BBB, then make heptane bottoms in BBBT and nonane bottoms in BBBB.
Push heptane overhead in BBB (octane tops in BBBB), sharpen CH/heptane in BBBT, and add a column to split nC6/MCP off cyclohexane for a pure CH bottoms.
Push CH out of heptane bottoms in BBBT (heptane worth ~$420M), sharpen C8/C9 split and heptane removal for octane tops.
Push heptane out of BBBB (octane tops to 95%), and sharpen BBBT so heptane bottoms reach premium 99%.
BBB failed with the turn-20 settings, so go back to the best design (turn 19) and read its streams in full.
Try for 99% premium heptane in BBBTB (more stages/boilup in BBBT) and purer nonane in BBBBB (more stages/reflux in BBBB), leaving BBB as it is.
Go back to the turn-19 best design and read its streams before making further changes.
Add small polishing columns: strip heptane from octane tops (BBBBT, worth ~$110M if 95%) and strip CH from heptane (BBBTB) toward 99% premium.
Split C5 mix (678M) into isopentane tops (~560M+) and n-pentane bottoms (~264M if 95%).
C5 split loses money (nC5 bottoms contaminated by 2,2-DMB, BT column costly); go back to turn-24 best and look at margins.
Push MCP/nC6 out of cyclohexane bottoms (98% -> 99% premium, ~+$55M) with a cheap polishing column change.
Push octane out of nonane bottoms toward 99% premium (+~$40M) with more stages/boilup in BBBB.
Both T products have room under the 95% blend spec (about 98% each), so cut reflux and boil-up in T to lower its $104M cost.
BBB costs $144M; try lower reflux/boil-up, relying on polishing columns downstream.
Turn 30's cheaper BBB made the downstream products less pure, so go back to the turn-29 best design and read its streams.
BB is the costliest column ($181M); try a double effect (HP at 6.75 bar, LP near 1 bar) so the HP C6 condenser heats the LP C7+ reboiler.
BBB likely failed from too low pressure after the LP-mixed BB bottoms (~1 bar, dp 0.7); run BBB with no valve and lower downstream valve drops to keep similar pressures.
Double-effect BB saved ~$75M on BB but downstream purities fell; go back to the turn-29 best to read its exact settings before redoing the double effect carefully.
Redo double-effect BB (HP 6.75 bar, LP 1.35 bar) with ~10% more reflux/boil-up to keep the BBT/BBB split sharp, and set BBB's valve so it runs near its old ~0.8 bar.
Hexane leaks into BBB (6%) with double-effect BB; raise BB reflux/boil-up to sharpen nC6/CH split while keeping heat-integration savings.
Double-effect BB keeps hurting downstream purity; go back to the turn-29 best design (4.064) and read its streams to find remaining margins.
Modest (~8%) trim of BBB reflux/boil-up to cut its $144M cost without the big purity loss seen in turn 30.
Back to best (turn 29) and trim feed column reflux/boil-up ~8% to cut its $130M cost; C4/C5 split looks very sharp (0% iC5 in TB).
Feed column failed when I trimmed it, so go back to the turn-29 best and read its streams before trying anything else.
Trim the C8/C9 column's reflux and boil-up to cut its $35M cost. The downstream octane polisher can absorb some loss of sharpness.
Pure iC5 (0.0506) is worth more than the C5 mix (0.0356), and nC5 alone is worth less than the mix. So split part of the iC5 off as tops and leave a C5-mix bottoms that still qualifies.
Revert to best; split C5 into a high-purity iC5 tops (~240 mol/s) and keep the bottoms large enough (~450) that 2,2-DMB stays under 5%, so it still sells as C5 mix.
Push the remaining ~7 mol/s nC4 out of the feed bottoms (into C4 mix TB, which has slack) so BTT iC5 can approach 99% premium.
Turn-44 change made column B fail to converge. Going back to the turn-43 best (4.188) to re-read its streams.
Add a small nC4 stripper on the 97% iC5 stream so the bottoms can reach 99% premium (+~$70M/yr).
Sharpen nC6/MCP split in BB with more stages (not reflux) so ~35 mol/s hexane goes to C6 paraffin blend instead of being lost in BBBTTT.
Return to the best design and trim the expensive BB column ($183M) by about 8% on reflux and boil-up to test how sensitive the downstream purity is.
Last turn's 8% trim of BB paid off, so trim another ~6% to see if the C6 paraffin blend stays above 95%.
Trim BB another ~6%; C6 paraffin blend at ~96% still has some slack.
Keep trimming BB (~5%), since the C6 paraffin blend still sits around 96%.
Continue trimming BB ~4%; the C6 paraffin blend still sits at about 96%.
Last BB trim went too far, so go back to the best design. Also trim boil-up on the $145M BBB column by 10% to see if the downstream polishers can absorb it.
Cutting BBB's boil-up broke the nonane and octane purities. Go back to the best design (turn 51) and re-read its streams.
Try splitting the C4 mix into premium iC4 and nC4 (worth ~+$58M/yr gross), after pushing more propane overhead in T.
Strip the ~18 mol/s propane out of the 84% iC4 stream so the bottoms sells as pure iC4 (worth ~$49-58M/yr) for a small column cost.
Trim BBB reflux+boilup together (keeping the cut point) to cut its $145M cost; recover more iC4 in TBT bottoms by shrinking the propane tops.
Turn 57's BBB/TBT trims lowered the reward, so return to the best design (turn 56) and look at it again.
Trim the $86M T column (C3/C4 split) by about 12% on both reflux and boil-up. The C3 blend and the C4 downstream still seem to have some slack.
Last turn's T trim paid off, so trim T another ~10%. The C3 blend is at 98%, so there is still slack.
Turn 60's T trim pushed propane into the iC4 stream, so go back to turn 59. Also try trimming the $145M BBB by 10% on reflux and boil-up together, with 10 more stages to hold purity.
Turn 61's BBB trim paid off, so trim BBB by another ~7% on reflux and boil-up together.
Turn 62's second BBB trim lost value, so go back to the turn 61 best. Then trim the $131M feed column by ~6% on reflux and boil-up.
Go back to the turn 61 best. The 6% trim on the feed column made column B fail, so try a smaller trim of about 3%.
Trimming the feed column makes B fail, so go back to the turn 61 best and look at its streams before trying other changes.
Try a double effect on the $144M BB column (C6/C7+ split): HP column at about 6.75 bar, LP column at about 1 bar, so the HP condenser can drive the LP reboiler.
The BB double effect saves about $57M/yr, but BBB failed, probably because its feed now arrives near 1 bar from the LP column. So run BBB with no valve drop and cut the drops of the columns below it.
The double effect lost a lot of downstream value because the C6/C7 cut moved. Go back to the turn 61 best and look at its streams before deciding whether to retune the double effect.
BTB C5 blend sits right at 95% because of 2,2-DMB leaking from B. Sharpen B (more stages and reflux, same vapour difference) to push DMB into BB, so BT can then send more iC5 to the premium tops.
Turn 69's sharper B failed to converge, so go back to the turn 61 best (4.404) and look at its streams before trying anything else.
Retry BB double effect with pressures closer to the original (HP ~4 bar, LP ~1.35 bar) so the C6/C7 cut moves less, and keep everything below it unchanged.

Raise the HP pressure of the BB double effect (dp 0.2, about 5.4 bar) so its condenser runs more than 10 K hotter than the LP reboiler (383 K) and the heat link switches on. The LP side stays as it was so the cut moves as little as possible.
Double effect on BB saves ~$60M but leaves ~38 mol/s n-hexane in BBB, which ruins the cyclohexane cuts. Raise boil-up slightly to push more C6 paraffins overhead.
The BB double-effect variants keep losing value downstream or making BBB fail. Go back to the turn 61 best (4.404) and look at its streams before choosing the next change.
Push the ~38 mol/s n-hexane in BBB up into the C6 paraffin blend BBT (worth ~$48M/yr; it is currently lost in BBBTTT) by raising the BB boil-up a little on the single column.
Go back to the best design and cut the energy of the expensive BBB column (C7/C8 split, $130M/yr) by lowering its reflux and boil-up together by about 10%.
Lowering BBB reflux and boil-up last turn saved money, so lower them a bit more and check the C7/C8 cut still holds.
Lowering BBB reflux and boil-up has paid off twice, so cut them a bit more (2.6/5.4) and check the C7/C8 cut still holds.
Go back to the turn 77 best, then cut the energy of the C4 splitter TB (n-butane comes out 100%, so it has slack) by lowering reflux and boil-up together.
Go back to the turn 77 best and cut the energy of the feed column (C4/C5 split, $130M/yr) by lowering its reflux and boil-up.
The feed-column energy cut failed to converge, so go back to the turn 77 best (4.442) and look at its streams before trying anything else.
Cut the energy of the C5/C6 split column B ($107M/yr) by lowering its reflux and boil-up a little.
Lowering B's reflux and boil-up let the C5/C6 cut slip, so BTB went impure. Go back to the turn 77 best.

Push more isopentane overhead in BT into the premium cut, and strip the 2,2-DMB out of BTB with a small column so the remaining stream still qualifies as C5 mix; also sharpen TBT to recover more isobutane.
Go back to the turn 77 best and look at its streams before making more changes.
TBTT (39 mol/s, 60% propane / 40% isobutane) is worth nothing. Take less distillate with more stages so the tops reach 95% C3 mix and the lost isobutane goes back to the premium bottoms.
BTTB is premium with ~0 n-pentane, so there is slack: raise BT boil-up to send more isopentane overhead into the premium cut (each mol/s moved is worth ~$0.7M/yr more than in the C5 blend).

Stopping here. The best design is the turn 77/86 one, with a reward of 4.442. Every recent change either lowered the reward or made the design invalid: cutting energy in B, BBB and the feed column, and raising BT boil-up. The streams still sold for nothing are small, about 10–46 mol/s each, so recovering them is not worth the extra column cost.
